spec_match.rationale: Running one string through new URL(), anchor.href, new Request() and new WebSocket() is a real and interesting probe of the shared host parser, but all four entry points inside one Chromium build share that parser, so the intra-browser 'disagreement' the lede warns about is not actually producible here — the change's real interop story is Chrome versus other engines and server-side validators.

interactive.rationale: Live input re-compares on every keystroke, four preset buttons cover the interesting cases, and the table, agreement banner and detail all derive from real constructor calls (including a WebSocket that is closed immediately after the parse).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card says 'before this change they could disagree; the point of shipping it is that they no longer do' — but on this pre-157 build the demo itself shows all applicable parsers agreeing (on the wrong outcome), so the promised before-state never appears; the card describes cross-engine history as if it were visible in-page.

edge_cases.rationale: The WebSocket scheme restriction is handled with a clear not-applicable row, throw counting distinguishes all-rejected from all-parsed, and anchors' never-throwing nature is documented — but the all-parsed-same branch's copy is wrong on a pre-157 build (see open question), which is exactly the edge this browser exercises.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5083335148437504 and the WPT WebSockets results the change was motivated by.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the URL and WebSocket-URL host contracts this page relies on and ran with the expected 6 pass / 2 fail pre-157 split on Chromium 141; partial carries the suite-level flag on the percent-encoded-space assertion recorded in the host-parser critique.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the initial comparison genuinely ran (console '"https://exa mple.com/path" -> 1 distinct answers across 3 parsers') and the screenshots show all three applicable parsers resolving exa%20mple.com with the green agreement banner — live pre-157 evidence; preset buttons and typing judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires parsers-compared with distinct/ran/threw counts on every comparison including the observed initial one; console is clean.

design_system.rationale: Layout and controls follow the design system, but the emerald agreement banner text (~3.7:1 on stone) repeats the shared palette AA shortfall at its bold normal size.

accessibility.rationale: The input is labelled, the outcome narrative is an aria-live=polite output, the table has a caption and row headers per parser, and agreement is stated in text alongside the aria-hidden icon.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: preset buttons wrap, the three-column table compresses via overflow-wrap:anywhere, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: Green 'agree' verdict endorses the pre-157 wrong outcome
openQuestions.detail: On this Chromium 141 build the default space-in-host string parses in all three applicable parsers, and the page shows a green check with 'Every parser resolved the same host. This is the state the change was made to guarantee.' That is misleading twice: agreement-on-accepting is precisely the pre-157 bug the feature removes, and the change guarantees consistent rejection, not this. When every parser parses a string whose authority contains a forbidden host code point, the banner and detail should say so ('all agree — but on a spec-forbidden host; Chrome 157 rejects this everywhere'), reusing the forbidden-code-point check the sibling pages already have.

openQuestions.title: Reframe the disagreement premise or demonstrate a real one
openQuestions.detail: All four entry points in one Chromium build share one host parser, so the in-page comparison can essentially never disagree with itself; the disagreement that motivated the change is between Chrome and other engines/servers (the wpt.fyi links). Either reframe the lede/card to say the page proves internal consistency while pointing at the cross-engine matrix, or add a fifth 'URL Standard says' row computed from the forbidden-code-point set so a genuine mismatch (this browser vs the spec) is visible on pre-157 builds.

openQuestions.title: Emerald banner text misses WCAG AA
openQuestions.detail: Shared palette finding: --accent-emerald on --bg-stone is ~3.7:1 for the bold banner text, below 4.5:1. Same as the sibling pages; a palette-level fix clears all instances.

summary: Mechanically sound — four real constructor calls, an immediately-closed WebSocket, honest not-applicable handling — and it produced live pre-157 evidence in this session: Chromium 141 resolved the space-in-host string identically (exa%20mple.com) through URL, anchor and Request. But that very result exposes the page's framing problem: the green banner congratulates agreement that is in fact the pre-157 bug, and the promised parser disagreement cannot occur inside one build that shares a single host parser. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/disallow-spaces-in-non-file-url-hosts/parser-agreement/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). The weakest of this feature's four pages: fix the banner semantics and either reframe or genuinely demonstrate the disagreement story.
